methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates eight cohorts and multiple orthogonal modalities (scRNA-seq, BCR-seq, bulk RNA-seq, mIHC, spatial transcriptomics, seromics, ELISpot, ELISA, survival datasets totaling ~1,582 patients), providing a strong discovery-plus-validation design. Statistical choices are appropriate: Dirichlet regression with log-likelihood tests, Wilcoxon rank-sum, moderated t-tests, with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction and Moran's I for trajectory analyses. Important limitations are acknowledged by the authors (small pretreatment biopsies, scBCR-seq restricted to 6 patients in D1, only 4 responders vs 8 non-responders in bulk analysis, FDR<0.2 thresholds used in V2). No power calculation is reported, blinding of mIHC community detection is not described, and antigen specificity of expanded PCs is unverified—weaknesses recognized in the Discussion. Overall rigor is solid for a translational multi-omic correlative study.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a correlative biomarker/mechanistic study nested within prospective neoadjuvant ICB trials (NCT03916627) plus retrospective analysis of several external cohorts, including randomized trial material (IMbrave150, POPLAR, OAK) and TCGA. By Oxford CEBM, this maps to 2b (individual cohort/biomarker analyses of trial material), not 1b because no new interventional comparison is tested. Clinical relevance is high: identifies IgG1+ PC skewing and CTA-targeting IgG1 antibodies as candidate predictive/response biomarkers for anti-PD-(L)1 and anti-PD-1/VEGF-A regimens, with survival corroboration across SKCM, NSCLC trials, and HCC. Endpoints combine pathological response (≥50% necrosis) and OS, both patient-relevant. Findings suggest actionable directions (CTA vaccination + ICB, IL-6/TNF/CD70 modulation) but are not yet practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the most applicable framework given the biomarker/prognostic focus; STROBE elements also apply. Methods document cohort composition, assay protocols (ELISA, ELISpot, seromics, scRNA-seq, mIHC pipeline), analytical software versions, and statistical approaches in detail. Patient-flow details are limited (no CONSORT-style diagram, limited reporting of missing data per modality, selection and attrition from the parent trials sparsely described), and biomarker cutoffs (e.g., 'high' vs 'low' IGHG1) are not explicitly pre-specified. Data availability is strong: multiple public identifiers cited (dbGaP phs001680.v1.p1, PRJNA489548, EGAS00001007547, GSE151530, GSE238264) and a Zenodo deposit (ref 61) for code/data. Reporting Summary is referenced per Nature Portfolio.

novelty_literature.justification: The paper extends prior work linking B cells/PCs/TLSs to ICB response (Helmink 2020, Petitprez 2020, Patil 2022, Laumont & Nelson 2023) by focusing specifically on IgG1 isotype skewing, clonal tracking between tumor and draining lymph node, and CTA-directed IgG1 antibody responses correlated with CD8+ T cell IFNγ. The combination of paired scBCR-seq + seromics + ELISpot + spatial/mIHC in neoadjuvant HCC and cross-tumor-type survival validation is a meaningful empirical and methodological advance. However, individual components (B cell/PC prognostic value, NY-ESO-1 antibody correlations with ICB, TLS importance) are incremental extensions rather than first-in-class discoveries; the mechanistic signaling (IL-6, ERN1/XBP1, CyPA, Midkine) is largely referential.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured with a clear discovery–validation narrative, informative abstract that is quantitatively grounded (38 patients, 7 validation cohorts, 500 scRNA-seq patients, 1,582 survival patients), and detailed figure legends that stand alone. Section flow follows a logical arc from cell-type enrichment → clonal tracking → spatial validation → serology → survival → mechanism. Minor issues: some figure captions are dense and mix results with methods; Fig. 5c–d description is unusually narrative; a few sentences in the Discussion are repetitive ('Combined, these findings suggest that PCs of responders have active effector function...'). Terminology and acronyms are generally defined on first use.

key_strengths: Multi-modal integration (scRNA-seq, paired scBCR-seq, bulk RNA-seq, mIHC, spatial transcriptomics, seromics against ~20,000 antigens, ELISpot) in neoadjuvant HCC with orthogonal confirmation of IgG1+ PC enrichment in responders
Discovery-plus-validation across eight cohorts spanning HCC, melanoma, NSCLC, with survival corroboration (~1,582 patients) including randomized trial material (POPLAR, OAK, IMbrave150)
Clonal tracking of CDR3-shared IgG1 clones between tumor and draining lymph node, plus linkage of circulating NY-ESO-1 IgG to CD8+ IFNγ responses
Appropriate statistics with FDR correction (Dirichlet regression, Wilcoxon, moderated t-tests, Moran's I); public data accessions and Zenodo code deposit cited
Clear translational framing: candidate predictive biomarker and rational combination strategy (CTA vaccination + ICB; IL-6/TNF/ERN1/CD70 modulation)
key_concerns: Small discovery sample sizes for several key analyses: scBCR-seq in only 6 D1 patients (2R/4NR); bulk RNA-seq in 12 patients (4R/8NR); ELISpot in effectively one responder/one non-responder—limits generalizability
No power calculation; some validation findings reported at relaxed FDR<0.2; biomarker cutoff definitions for 'high' vs 'low' IGHG1 in survival analyses not clearly pre-specified
Antigen specificity of clonally expanded tumor PCs is not functionally validated (acknowledged by authors)
Patient-flow details (selection, attrition, missing data per modality) are sparse; no CONSORT/REMARK diagram
Mechanistic claims (IL-6, CyPA/Midkine, ERN1/XBP1) rely on CellChat-inferred ligand–receptor signaling and pseudotime, without perturbational validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: A comprehensive, methodologically careful multi-cohort translational study that establishes IgG1+ plasma cell skewing and CTA-directed IgG1 antibodies as correlates of ICB response with cross-tumor survival support. Scope, novelty of the humoral-cellular axis framing, and depth of validation justify consideration at Tier 1; remaining concerns are around small per-modality n, unvalidated antigen specificity, and biomarker pre-specification, which fit minor revisions.
